commands.description: Open the interactive TUI (default when no command is supplied).
commands.details: Capture enabled chats while connected; --offline browses the local archive. An interactive terminal is required.

commands.description: Alias for tui.
commands.details: Capture continues until exit; --offline browses without connecting.

commands.description: Run headless capture and the loopback API.
commands.details: --offline serves the local archive without connecting. Cannot be combined with --no-api. Keep this or the TUI running for owner-channel commands.

commands.description: Link WhatsApp and set wasync up in your browser, without a terminal.
commands.details: Starts wasync like serve and opens a local page that shows the QR code to scan, lets you choose chats to keep, connects an agent (saving its credential straight where whatsapp-axi reads it, never showing it) and can start wasync when you log in. It keeps running as the capture owner until you press Ctrl-C. If wasync is already running it opens the setup page of the running copy instead. The page never opens by a printed link. Connecting an agent and turning on start-at-login ask for Touch ID or your password (macOS) or Windows Hello or your password (Windows); where this computer cannot show that prompt the page shows the terminal command instead.

commands.description: Start wasync by itself when you log in.
commands.details: install adds a login item for your account only (a macOS LaunchAgent or a Windows startup item; no administrator rights) that runs wasync serve with this data directory; it takes effect at the next login. It needs an interactive terminal, a typed confirmation and, where available, the system prompt (Touch ID or password; Windows Hello or password). uninstall removes it. status says whether it is installed. Linux is not set up.

commands.description: Pair by QR or reuse the saved session, discover groups, then open the TUI.
commands.details: In an interactive terminal a successful login opens the TUI with capture for enabled groups, as plain wasync does. --select=false or --observe keeps the diagnostic output instead: a group table, with an optional selection prompt when --select=true. --select defaults to terminal interactivity. --observe defaults to 0 and counts events without saving message bodies. Without a terminal, login prints the group table and exits; use tui or serve for capture.

commands.description: Unlink the saved WhatsApp device session.
commands.details: Connects to WhatsApp when a saved session exists. Local archives and chat preferences remain on disk.

commands.description: Discover and select group chats for capture.
commands.details: Use help groups list, help groups enable, or help groups disable.

commands.description: List cached groups and capture preferences.
commands.details: --refresh connects using the saved session to refresh metadata; otherwise reads local state.

commands.description: Persist capture preference for one group or all cached groups.
commands.details: Enabling queues best-effort history when capture runs; it cannot guarantee a complete archive. Example: wasync groups enable '123456789@g.us'

commands.description: Disable capture for one group or all cached groups.
commands.details: Previously archived messages remain local.

commands.description: Manage capture for groups and direct chats.
commands.details: Direct-chat discovery is best effort, not a complete WhatsApp inbox listing.

commands.description: List cached groups and direct chats.
commands.details: --refresh connects to refresh group metadata; direct chats are discovered from delivered events.

commands.description: Persist capture preference for one chat or all cached chats.
commands.details: An explicit direct-chat ID can be added. Enabling does not start a background process: keep tui or serve running.

commands.description: Disable capture for one chat or all cached chats.
commands.details: Previously archived messages remain local.

commands.description: Capture now, reusing a running owner when available.
commands.details: --wait defaults to 30s, allowed 0 to 60s. --history requests best-effort history for enabled chats; --chat restricts it. History needs a known message anchor and phone availability; a successful request does not imply full recovery.

commands.description: Configure automatic media downloads or download one attachment.
commands.details: Use help media policy or help media download. No fixed application media-size cap; WhatsApp transfer limits and remote availability apply.

commands.description: Read or persist a per-chat media policy; returns JSON.
commands.details: auto downloads media on future deliveries, including delivered history; manual requires an explicit download; inherit follows --download-media / WASYNC_DOWNLOAD_MEDIA. Omit --mode to read the saved policy. This setting persists across restarts and does not bulk-download older archived messages or enable capture.

commands.description: Queue a one-time attachment download; returns JSON.
commands.details: Requires a running connected tui or serve owner with its command channel, enabled capture, and retained download metadata. Does not change the saved policy. Older archives may lack the metadata, and WhatsApp may no longer serve the attachment.

commands.description: Explicitly send a text message or local attachment.
commands.details: At least --text or --file is required. With a file, --text is the caption and --type defaults to document; image supports JPEG/PNG. Reuses a running owner or connects with the saved session. A server acknowledgement is not proof of recipient delivery; do not automatically retry uncertain sends.

commands.description: Quote an archived message in a reply.
commands.details: The target must already be in the local archive of that chat. --mention (repeatable, up to 20) takes a user JID such as 123456789@s.whatsapp.net and the text must contain @123456789 so the mention is visible. Reuses a running owner or connects with the saved session. A server acknowledgement is not proof of recipient delivery; do not automatically retry uncertain sends.

commands.description: React to an archived message, or clear your reaction.
commands.details: The target must already be in the local archive of that chat. --emoji takes one emoji; --remove clears the reaction you gave earlier; give exactly one of them. WhatsApp keeps one reaction per person per message, so a new emoji replaces the old one. Reuses a running owner or connects with the saved session. A server acknowledgement is not proof of delivery; do not automatically retry uncertain sends.

commands.description: Replace the text of one of your own sent messages.
commands.details: The target must already be in the local archive of that chat, be a text message you sent, and still be inside WhatsApp's edit window (about 20 minutes after it was first sent); otherwise nothing is sent and the error says why. Reuses a running owner or connects with the saved session. A server acknowledgement is not proof that recipients saw the change; do not automatically retry uncertain sends.

commands.description: Request deletion from the local archive only.
commands.details: Requires a running owner. Returns an approval request without deleting anything. A human must approve through the TUI or interactive actions approve; there is no --yes.

commands.description: Request a WhatsApp deletion with human approval.
commands.details: everyone requests revocation of your own message, subject to WhatsApp limits. my-whatsapp-chat deletes your WhatsApp chat state and leaves the local archive. Requires a running owner and subsequent human approval; there is no --yes.
commands.usage:
delete --chat CHAT_ID --scope everyone --message-id MESSAGE_ID
       wasync delete --chat CHAT_ID --scope my-whatsapp-chat

commands.description: Inspect or interactively approve a destructive request or an agent's chat access request.
commands.details: Requires the running owner's command channel. REQUEST_ID is the 32-character hexadecimal ID returned by clean or delete, or printed by whatsapp-axi access request.

commands.description: Show or change how agents get chats: ask each time (default) or sync all chats.
commands.details: Human only: changing it needs an interactive terminal, a typed confirmation and a running owner; there is no --yes. ask makes every agent request wait for your approval. all turns on capture for every chat (--history now = from now on only, full = full history sync) and approves an agent's read, send, reply and react request for the one chat it matched at once, without asking, so agents can discover any chat by name or number (a name probe both reveals and grants it); editing its own messages and deleting stay manual. Switching back to ask stops future automatic approvals and keeps access already given.

commands.description: Show or change how agents get chats.
commands.details: Without an argument the current mode is printed. Changing it asks for a typed SYNC ALL (or ASK) and needs the TUI or serve running.

commands.description: List the requests waiting for you, with what each asks for.
commands.details: Requires an interactive terminal and the running owner's command channel. Shows the agent, whether it asks to read or also send, and the candidate chats, so run it yourself; the serve console line carries only the agent name and request ID.

commands.description: Read the status of a pending or completed request as JSON.
commands.details: Does not approve or execute the request.

commands.description: Ask a human to approve a pending destructive request or chat access request.
commands.details: Requires an interactive terminal and a typed confirmation. Agents cannot bypass confirmation with --yes. For a chat access request you also choose the chat (when several match) and the history depth: from now on only, or a full history sync.

commands.description: Open the approval page in your browser.
commands.details: Shows what agents are waiting on and lets you choose between asking each time and syncing all chats, without a terminal. Needs the TUI or serve running. The link works once for two minutes. Each approval still asks for Touch ID or your password (macOS) or Windows Hello or your password (Windows) and names exactly what you are approving; where this computer cannot show that prompt, the page only lists requests. The link is never printed.

commands.description: Inspect saved local pairing state and cached groups.
commands.details: Does not check network connectivity. For read-only agent queries while capture runs, prefer query status.

commands.description: Read-only JSON queries for agents, without an API or WhatsApp connection.
commands.details: Use help query messages or help query search for filters and pagination. All results are JSON; exit codes: 0 success (including empty items), 1 error, 130 cancellation. Queries never download media. Also: query version, message, thread, changes, checkpoint and doctor (see help query COMMAND). --v1 on groups, chats, messages, search, status and message emits the versioned v1 envelope; version, thread, changes, checkpoint and doctor always use it.

commands.description: Read cached group summaries as JSON.
commands.details: --enabled restricts results to enabled groups. No WhatsApp connection or running owner required.

commands.description: Read cached group and direct-chat summaries as JSON.
commands.details: --enabled restricts results to enabled chats. No WhatsApp connection or running owner required. --v1 emits the v1 envelope; with --v1, --match QUERY resolves a chat by JID or name (v1 only).

commands.description: Read archived messages as paginated JSON, newest first.
commands.details: --group is a legacy alias for --chat; do not combine them. --since is inclusive, --until exclusive. --limit is 1 to 200 (default 50). Reuse next_cursor with identical filters; empty items is success. Never downloads attachments.
commands.usage: query messages --chat CHAT_ID [--since RFC3339] [--until RFC3339] [--sender SENDER_ID] [--limit N] [--cursor CURSOR] [--json]

commands.description: Search archived text and captions using SQLite FTS; returns JSON.
commands.details: Quote PHRASE as one argument (maximum 1024 bytes). --group is a legacy alias for --chat. Dates are inclusive --since and exclusive --until; --limit is 1 to 200 (default 50). Pass next_cursor with identical filters. Does not index document bodies or download media. --v1 emits the v1 envelope; with --v1, --context N (0 to 5) adds messages before and after each hit (v1 only).
commands.usage: query search PHRASE [--chat CHAT_ID] [--since RFC3339] [--until RFC3339] [--sender SENDER_ID] [--limit N] [--cursor CURSOR] [--json]

commands.description: Read persisted sync observations as JSON.
commands.details: Current network connectivity is unknown; reconnects do not prove missed messages were recovered.

commands.description: Report API, build and archive schema versions as a v1 envelope.
commands.details: Report API, build and schema versions as a v1 envelope without opening the archive for writes. Always emits the v1 envelope; --v1 is accepted and ignored.

commands.description: Read one archived message by its stable reference; returns JSON.
commands.details: REF is an account-scoped m1_... reference from v1 results. References survive restarts, purge and re-capture; local row ids do not. Expired content is never returned; revoked messages return their tombstone. With --v1 the data is the v1 message shape (legacy fields plus ref and chat_kind).

commands.description: Read a message with surrounding context from its chat as a v1 envelope.
commands.details: Returns REF as anchor with up to --before earlier and --after later messages (0 to 20 each, default 5) from the same chat, oldest first. Always emits the v1 envelope. Expired content is never returned; revoked messages return their tombstone.

commands.description: Read the change journal of the current account as a v1 envelope, oldest first.
commands.details: Entries list sequence, cursor, op, chat_id, message_id and a message ref, never message content. Pass page.next_cursor (c1_...) to --after; omit --after to start from the oldest retained change. --limit is 1 to 1000 (default 100). cursor_expired means the cursor is older than the 30-day retention or from another archive or account: resnapshot. Offline reads cannot commit checkpoints; commit through the running owner's API (PUT /api/v1/checkpoints/{consumer}, scope observe).

commands.description: Read a consumer's committed change-journal checkpoint as a v1 envelope.
commands.details: NAME is 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -. Read only: committing is a write and goes through the running owner's API (PUT /api/v1/checkpoints/{consumer}, scope observe).

commands.description: Report installation, data directory, archive, pairing, owner and agent checks as a v1 envelope.
commands.details: Each check is pass, warn or fail with a fix command. Never connects to WhatsApp or the network and never creates or changes files. An owner is detected by probing device.lock without holding it; its live connection state is available only from GET /api/v1/health/deep.

commands.description: Manage scoped credentials for agents using the local /api/v1.
commands.details: Human only: grant and revoke must be run by a human in an interactive terminal and require typing the client name; there is no --yes, and none of these commands is available over the API. They edit agents.json in the data directory, work whether or not an owner is running (a running owner reloads changes), and never connect to WhatsApp. Use help agents grant, help agents list, or help agents revoke.

commands.description: Create a scoped agent credential; human only, interactive terminal required.
commands.details: NAME is 1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -. Scopes: read.chats, read.messages, read.media, observe, send, react, edit.own, chat.state, group.admin, capture.manage, export (default read.chats,read.messages). There is no destructive scope. send, react, edit.own, chat.state, group.admin and capture.manage need a chat list: normally use --on-demand, which starts the client with no chats: it asks (whatsapp-axi access request) and you approve each chat, read and send separately, with a history depth, in the TUI or actions approve. --chat (repeatable) pre-approves a chat by name (shown with its JID and confirmed by you) or by JID. --rate is requests per minute (default 60); omit --expires for no expiry. grant offers to save the credential where whatsapp-axi reads it; if you decline it is printed once; only its hash is stored. Legacy api.token, send.token and approve.token are never accepted as agent credentials.
commands.usage: agents grant NAME [--scope S1,S2] [--chat NAME ...] [--on-demand] [--expires DURATION] [--rate N]

commands.description: List agent clients, scopes and limits.
commands.details: Never prints credentials or hashes. Does not require an interactive terminal.

commands.description: Revoke an agent credential; human only, interactive terminal required.
commands.details: Requires typing the client name to confirm; there is no --yes. A running owner reloads the change.

commands.description: Push identifier-only change notifications to HTTPS endpoints.
commands.details: Human only: every subcommand (add, list, remove, test, deadletter) must be run by a human in an interactive terminal; there is no --yes, no agent scope, and no API route. Events never carry message text; receivers fetch content through the scoped /api/v1. Delivery runs while tui or serve is running. Use help webhooks add, help webhooks list, help webhooks remove, help webhooks test, or help webhooks deadletter.

commands.description: Register a webhook endpoint and print its signing secret once; human only.
commands.details: HTTPS with a public hostname only; loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade NAT and metadata addresses are refused, redirects are not followed. --chat (repeatable) and --op limit events. Requires typing the endpoint name; there is no --yes. The secret is also stored in webhooks.json, readable only by your OS user.
commands.usage: webhooks add NAME --url https://HOST/PATH [--chat CHAT_JID ...] [--op OP,OP]

commands.description: List webhook endpoints, filters and status.
commands.details: Never prints signing secrets. Requires an interactive terminal because endpoint URLs may carry tokens.

commands.description: Stop delivery to an endpoint and delete its secret; human only.
commands.details: Requires typing the endpoint name; there is no --yes. A running owner reloads the change.

commands.description: Send a signed ping event to an endpoint now; human only.
commands.details: Uses the same SSRF-guarded sender as delivery and reports the outcome. Requires an interactive terminal.

commands.description: List events that could not be delivered, or empty the list.
commands.details: Entries are identifiers and outcomes only. Requires an interactive terminal because entries include endpoint URLs and chat IDs.

commands.description: Show installed build information.
commands.details: Also available as wasync --version.

commands.description: Discover all commands without connecting or opening the archive.
commands.details: Use wasync COMMAND [SUBCOMMAND] --help as an alternative. --json emits a versioned command catalog, root help, and query conventions. Global flags precede the command.

query_help:
Usage: wasync [--data-dir PATH] query COMMAND

  groups [--enabled] [--json]
  chats [--enabled] [--json]
  messages --chat CHAT_ID [--since RFC3339] [--until RFC3339]
           [--sender SENDER_ID] [--limit 50] [--cursor CURSOR] [--json]
  search "phrase" [--chat CHAT_ID] [--since RFC3339] [--until RFC3339]
           [--sender SENDER_ID] [--limit 50] [--cursor CURSOR] [--json]
  status [--json]
  version [--json]
  message --ref REF [--json]
  thread --ref REF [--before 5] [--after 5] [--json]
  changes [--after CURSOR] [--limit 100] [--json]
  checkpoint --consumer NAME [--json]
  doctor [--json]

All results are JSON. Queries read the existing archive without connecting to
WhatsApp, requiring an API, or stopping the TUI. Dates are inclusive --since and
exclusive --until; results are newest first. Pass next_cursor to --cursor with
the same filters for the next page. An empty items array is a successful result.
Status describes persisted observations; current network connectivity is unknown.
Global flags precede query. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 130 cancellation.

--v1 wraps groups, chats, messages, search, status and message results in the
versioned v1 envelope; version, thread, changes, checkpoint and doctor always
use it. v1 only: chats --match QUERY resolves a chat by JID or name, and
search --context N (0 to 5) adds messages around each hit. message and thread
take stable m1_ references; changes reads the change journal (c1_ cursors) and
checkpoint reads a consumer checkpoint (commit through the owner's API).
Use wasync help query COMMAND for details.
root_help:
wasync — personal WhatsApp group sync client

Usage: wasync [--data-dir PATH] [--timeout 3m] [--api-addr 127.0.0.1:8787] [--no-api] COMMAND

  tui [--offline]                            Full-screen group browser and capture (default)
  run                                        Start the TUI with capture
  serve [--offline]                          Headless capture and local API
  setup                                      Link WhatsApp and choose chats in your browser, no terminal
  service install|uninstall|status           Start wasync by itself when you log in
  login [--select=true|false] [--observe 30s]  Pair or reuse session, then open the TUI
  logout                                     Unlink device; preserve cached groups
  groups list [--refresh] [--json]            List cached groups; optionally connect
  groups enable GROUP_ID|--all               Enable selected or all cached groups
  groups disable GROUP_ID|--all              Disable capture preference
  chats list|enable|disable                   Manage group and direct chat capture
  clean --chat CHAT_ID (--message-id ID|--all)  Request local cleanup; human CLI/TUI approval
  delete --chat CHAT_ID --scope SCOPE        Request WhatsApp deletion; human CLI/TUI approval
  sync [--wait 30s] [--history] [--chat ID]    Capture now, reusing any running owner
  actions list                               Requests waiting for you (interactive)
  access mode [ask|all]                      How agents get chats: ask each time or sync all
  actions approve REQUEST_ID                 Interactive typed approval, no --yes
  approvals                                  Open the approval page in your browser
  actions status REQUEST_ID                  Inspect a pending/completed request
  media policy --chat ID [--mode auto|manual|inherit]  Saved per-chat media setting
  media download --chat ID --message-id ID    One-time attachment download (live owner)
  send --to CHAT_ID [--text TEXT] [--file PATH --type image|document]
  reply --chat CHAT_ID --message-id ID --text TEXT [--mention USER_JID ...]
  react --chat CHAT_ID --message-id ID (--emoji EMOJI|--remove)
  edit --chat CHAT_ID --message-id ID --text TEXT
  status                                     Inspect local pairing state
  query [groups|chats|messages|search|status]       Read-only JSON queries for agents
  query [version|message|thread|changes|checkpoint|doctor]  More queries; --v1 envelope
  agents grant|list|revoke                   Scoped agent credentials; human, interactive
  webhooks add|list|remove|test|deadletter   HTTPS change notifications; human, interactive
  version                                    Show installed build information
  help [COMMAND [SUBCOMMAND]]                 Detailed command help, without connecting
  help --json                                Machine-readable command catalog for agents

Global flags (before COMMAND):
  --data-dir PATH          Dedicated private data directory
  --timeout 3m             Overall command timeout
  --api-addr HOST:PORT     Loopback API address (default 127.0.0.1:8787)
  --no-api                Disable the TUI API and command channel
  --download-media        Default automatic media downloads; per-chat policy overrides
  --pairing-full-history  Request fuller history on NEW pairing only (best effort)
  --version               Show installed build information

The TUI captures enabled groups and imports history when WhatsApp delivers it.
Non-interactive login and observation remain diagnostics and discard message bodies.
Global flags precede the command. Ctrl-C cancels network operations.
